subject: Renewal: burst bridge + invoice timing for CloudRetail
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@cloudretail.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Tran <alex.tran@cloudretail.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — burst credit ask and invoice timing

Soojin,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. CloudRetail is preparing our Q3 procurement plan and we want to lock the renewal terms for our inference footprint. A few points from our side: 

- Current monthly commit: 200M tokens (historical peak ~270M).
- We're planning a product launch in September that could push peak consumption for two quarters.
- Ask: a 12-month renewal with a 300M tokens/month commit and an ad-hoc burst credit of 50M tokens we can draw during the first 90 days after go-live.
- Financial ask: align invoicing to our fiscal cadence (Net 60) so the first invoice hits in Q4; we also prefer a 12-month price-hold at the negotiated rate.

Attached are our usage report for May and a draft SOW to help with scope. We can sign quickly if we have a clear burst-credit and invoice-timing confirmation — our procurement team needs a PO submitted by 2026-07-15.

Questions for you: What discount level can you offer on a 300M/month commit? Can Redwood accept Net 60 invoice terms? And can you document the burst-credit usage policy (exhaustion, replenishment)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if useful.

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Product Operations
CloudRetail

Attachments: usage_report_May2026.csv, SOW_draft.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cloudretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — burst credit ask and invoice timing

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Appreciate the PO timeline; we'll prioritize. High-level response and a counterproposal below.

Counterproposal (initial):
- Term: 12 months, effective on signature.
- Commit: 300M tokens / month.
- Unit economics: blended per-token rate $0.00085 (post-discount), equivalent to ~15% off list for the initial 12-month term.
- Burst credit: 40M tokens of one-time ad-hoc credit available during the first 90 days; additional bursts are billable at commit rate unless we agree on a top-up.
- Invoice terms: we can accept Net 60 for the first two invoices for onboarding/proration; treasury will need to approve ongoing Net 60 — ask submitted.
- Price-hold: 12 months guaranteed at the negotiated blended rate.
- SLA: 99.9% regional availability; credits for regressions per standard SLA appendix.

If CloudRetail signs up for a 24-month term we can improve to a blended rate of $0.00077 (~20% off) and increase the initial burst credit to 60M.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal approvals on our side (finance + legal) today — Marissa / Ben helping with the exceptions.
2) I’ll send a clean term sheet and a DocuSign link for signatures.
3) If procurement needs it, we can include a short policy doc for burst-credit consumption.

I’ve attached a term sheet draft (redwood_renewal_term_sheet_v1.pdf). Please let me know if the 40M burst + Net 60 (first two invoices) is acceptable or if we should route for the 24-month improved pricing.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_renewal_term_sheet_v1.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion — burst credit ask and invoice timing

Marissa/Ben — forwarding CloudRetail's ask and my initial counter. Deal id: CR-2026-089. Quick internal notes and questions: 

- Revenue motion: 300M/mo commit, likely upsell opportunity post-launch.
- They want 50M ad-hoc burst; I countered with 40M and Net 60 for first two invoices. Procurement needs PO by 2026-07-15.
- Can finance make an exception for Net 60 on this account for ongoing invoices (they've asked explicitly)? If not, can we accept Net 45 recurring and Net 60 for first two invoices as a compromise?
- Legal: if we increase burst credit to 50M or 60M for the 12-month term, what concessions should we require (prepayment, acceleration clause, or minimum ramp)?

Proposed internal offer to speed signing: 15% discount (blended $0.00080), 45M burst credit, Net 60 for first two invoices + Net 45 thereafter, 12-month price-hold. Approve?

I need thumbs by EOD 6/18 to hit procurement timeline. Thanks.

— Soojin

From: Elena Morales <elena@cloudretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Tran <alex.tran@cloudretail.com>, procurement@cloudretail.com
Date: 2026-06-22T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — burst credit ask and invoice timing

Soojin & team,

Appreciate the quick counter. A few clarifications and asks from procurement/legal: 

- Burst: CloudRetail's procurement prefers the full 50M burst credit if possible (we will not request additional ad-hoc credit in the first 6 months). The 45M suggest is reasonable if needed.
- Invoice timing: Net 60 is mandatory for our contracts — this is a hard requirement for the PO. We can escalate internally on our side if Redwood has alternatives (e.g., prepay ramp, escrow).
- SLA & credits: we need the 12-month price-hold and the SLA credit formula spelled out in the term sheet. If latency regressions cause production impact, we need rollback credits tied to QPS/latency breaches for the first 90 days after launch.
- Compliance: please include a link to SOC 2 evidence and any current pen-test summary to put in our procurement packet.

If you can confirm 50M burst + Net 60, we will prepare the PO and route for signature by 7/15. If 45M + Net 60 is the final, we will need a short waiver from finance on their side (timeline risk).

Thanks — we can do a short call tomorrow to finalize language.

Best,
Elena

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — burst credit ask and invoice timing

Elena — thank you. Internal approvals concluded and here are firm next steps we can commit to: 

1) Commercial: 12-month term, 300M tokens/month commit, blended rate $0.00080 (15% off list), price-hold for 12 months.
2) Burst credit: Redwood will provide a one-time 50M token burst credit during the first 90 days post-go-live. Policy: burst credit is a one-time bucket; if exhausted, additional consumption will be billed at the committed rate. We will include clear exhaustion alerts and a contact for emergency top-up.
3) Invoice terms: Redwood finance has approved Net 60 for the first three invoices for this deal to align with your PO timing. After that, Net 45 recurring unless the finance team approves ongoing Net 60 (we will continue follow-up).
4) SLA & credits: we will add an SLA appendix with a latency credit matrix for production-impacting regressions during go-live. This will be included in the term sheet.
5) Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and pen-test summary: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/CloudRetail-SOC2-evidence (link) — I’ll also attach the pointer in the DocuSign packet.

Next items I will do today:
- Upload the signed term sheet to DocuSign and send the link to your procurement team (pre-populated with PO fields).
- Send a short burst-credit policy doc and the SLA appendix for procurement/legal review.

DocuSign link (stub): https://docusign.example.com/abcd1234 — procurement should receive within the hour. Please confirm the PO route so we can tag the contract properly. Once the PO is in, we’ll bucket the burst credit and schedule the onboarding sequence.

Thanks everyone — excited to keep CloudRetail moving.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
